passage: Counsellor's note, Wednesday. Manjula (Class 10) arrived with a list of thirty jobs cut from a magazine. I asked her to put it aside and tell me how a working life would have to feel to suit her. She thought, then said: “Independence. A steady income. Work that helps people.” We wrote those three on the board. Only then did we test fields against them. Nursing and public health fitted well; teaching fitted; graphic design excited her but she was unsure about steady income. She said medicine sounds like helping but worried about the years it takes. I suggested she talk to people who do the work in the fields that stayed. She copied the three words into her diary. — Ojas

qa.q: What three things did Manjula say she wants from work?
qa.a: Independence, a steady income and work that helps people.

qa.q: What might Manjula have felt when asked to put her job list aside?
qa.a: A little surprised or unsure at first, but then engaged, since she quickly named what she wants.

qa.q: What could Manjula do next, and why?
qa.a: Talk to people who work in nursing, public health and teaching, because a real working day shows whether those fields truly match her values.

qa.q: How does the conversation look to Ojas?
qa.a: Ojas sees a student become clearer once the question changes from which job to what kind of life, so Ojas stays back and lets her lead.

grounding: A student asks what a good working life should feel like before naming jobs, then checks which fields match.

subtype: Approach: values-first reflection before naming jobs [Thinking]
passage:
Sunday

Everyone keeps asking what I want to "become". Doctor? Engineer? Naveen said IAS because it sounds impressive. I didn't have an answer, and it made me feel stupid.

So tonight I did it differently. Before any job names, I wrote: What should a good working life feel like for me?

I wrote three things. One: independence. I don't want someone watching every minute. Two: steady money, because I've seen Amma stress about rent. Three: helping people directly. I felt proud and warm helping at the free clinic camp last year.

Then I made a list of careers and checked each against those three. Doctor: helps people, steady, but long training. Physiotherapist: helps, fairly independent, steady. Pharmacy: steady, less direct help. Teacher: helps, steady.

I'm Anjali, and for the first time, I don't feel lost. I have a compass, not a destination.

qa.a: Independence, steady money and helping people directly.

qa.q: How did Anjali feel before writing the values down?
qa.a: Anjali felt stupid and lost when asked what to become.

qa.q: What else could Anjali do to test the careers that match?
qa.a: Anjali could talk to a physiotherapist or teacher about their daily work, to see if the values really fit in practice.

qa.q: How might Amma see Anjali's list?
qa.a: Amma might feel touched that her rent stress shaped Anjali's wish for steady income, and glad Anjali is thinking so carefully.

grounding: A diary shows a student asking what a good working life should feel like before naming careers, listing independence, steady income and helping people, then checking fields against them.

Anand: deep 😅
Anand: ok sorry. like what

Shreya: 2. steady income. no stress every month like we had after dad's shop closed
Shreya: 3. actually helping people. not just making money for some company
Anand: ok that's actually smart
Shreya: then I'll check each stall against those 3
Shreya: nursing: helping yes, steady yes, freedom meh
Shreya: counselling: helping yes, freedom yes, steady... need to ask
Anand: can I copy your list method lol
Shreya: make your own 3 🙂
Anand: ok mine are money, money, money
Shreya: anand 🙄

qa.a: Freedom, steady income and actually helping people.

qa.q: How did Shreya seem to feel about the career fair?
qa.a: Shreya seemed calm and focused, confident about going in with a clear method.

qa.q: What could Shreya ask at the counselling stall?
qa.a: Shreya could ask how steady the income is and what training is needed, since that is the value still unclear.

qa.q: How does the method look to Anand?
qa.a: Anand starts by joking but finds it smart, and wants to try it, even while joking about Anand's own three.
